hook.line: A step-by-step tutorial on how to use the new ChatGPT search.
hook.visual: Smiling woman cut out over her own blog post, pointing up at tilted blue 'OpenAI ChatGPT Search / step-by-step tutorial' tags and a yellow 'Press down 2x the speed' note.

beats.what: Promise of a step-by-step tutorial over the blog post's title card, with a 'watch at 2x' sticky note
Cut: background scrolls to how ChatGPT decides to search, and the manual 'search the web' button
Cut to the weather example screenshot pulled from the National Weather Service
Zoom punch on her face as the weather example lands
Cut: news, then sports and location (pizza near you) sections scroll behind her
Follow-up conversation example and availability caveat: paid users only for now
Cut to her kitchen, full frame, with a blue 'Sabrina.DEV' label for the newsletter CTA

why_it_works: The background is her own blog post scrolling in step with what she says, so the video doubles as a preview of the full guide she sells at the end
'Press down 2x the speed' note invites a replay at double speed, which counts as extra watch time
Fast 4 words/s delivery with 1-3 concrete examples (weather, news, pizza) keeps a dry feature list moving
Setting change at 30 s (blog to kitchen with a big name label) marks the CTA clearly as a different beat
weaknesses: The blog text behind her is tiny and mostly covered by her face, so the screenshots cannot be read on a phone
No spoken captions, so muted viewers only get the title tags
Video ends mid-sentence on the CTA
for_robert: Use the scene-change-for-CTA move: when he asks people to follow or click, cut to a new frame with a bold name label and have Fred hold the sign, so the ask reads as its own beat.
